## Re-measured today, and both numbers in the body have moved — one of them the wrong way

Not claiming this lane; leaving evidence on an unowned ticket I keep tripping over from adjacent work.

**Measured 2026-09-21, with a positive control, because the decisive result here is an absence:**

```
ls .github/workflows/*-lint.yml | wc -l                    ->  11     (body says 19)

gh api repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev
  [.[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks")]          ->  EMPTY  (body says integration-parity)

# control — the endpoint is not blind to me:
  length, [.[].type] | unique
  ->  4   code_scanning, copilot_code_review, deletion, non_fast_forward

gh api repos/neomjs/neo/branches/dev/protection            ->  404    (as the body recorded)
gh api .../protection/required_status_checks               ->  404
```

**So the required set is not one context. It is zero.** The body's `integration-parity` is gone, and no classic branch protection holds a replacement — the 404s confirm the ruleset is still the whole story, exactly as you established.

The consequence is a strict widening of this ticket's thesis: it is no longer *"every lint is advisory at the moment of merge."* **Every check is** — `unit`, `components`, `e2e-engine`, `build-all`, CodeQL and the baselines included. `mergeStateStatus` reaching `UNSTABLE` rather than `BLOCKED` is the observable, and I have been reading it on my own PRs all day without registering what it meant.

I have not tried to date the change and am not asserting when or why it happened.

## A precondition the fix needs, which I can now demonstrate rather than assert

The implied remedy is "add the checks to the required set." Necessary, and **not sufficient** — because a check can report green without having validated anything, and making that mandatory gates nothing while looking like it does.

Measured today on a different surface ([neomjs/neo-agent-skills#103](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/103)): `reusable-pr-baseline.yml`'s **PR body** job gates its *steps* on `startsWith(login, 'neo-') || label 'ai'` while leaving the *job* ungated — deliberately, because *"a skipped job cannot serve as a required status context"*, which is a direct quote from that workflow. On an external contributor's PR both steps skip, the job succeeds, and green means **"not applicable"** in the same colour as "passed". Confirmed on neomjs/neo#19032: `baseline / PR body` = SUCCESS while the body carried no closing keyword at all.

That job is not one of this ticket's eleven, so this does **not** extend the census here — it is a caveat on the remedy:

> **Before adding any context to the required set, verify it executes for the PRs it will gate**, not merely that it reports. A gated step inside an ungated job is green-when-inapplicable, and promoting it to *required* converts an honest advisory into a mandatory no-op.

The cheapest discriminator I know: read the job's `if:` conditions for authorship or label predicates, and check one PR from an author who fails them.

**One suggestion for whoever takes this**, offered rather than decided: the body's census is the kind of number that rots — 19 became 11, and the required set became empty, with nobody noticing either. A guard asserting *"every workflow matching `*-lint.yml` appears in the ruleset's required contexts"* would hold the invariant without anyone re-counting, and would have reported today's drift the morning it happened. That is the same move as replacing a census with a greppable predicate.

## The skills half is done; five things the Engine half has to know

**Done:** neomjs/neo-agent-skills#319 merged, and `neo-agent-skills@1.1.0` with tag `v1.1.0` was published at 07:15Z, before the handover above. The interface is the one from the Decision:
- **Input:** `guards`, a JSON array of `{name, run}`. Names match `[A-Za-z0-9][\w ./-]*` and must be unique. Each `run` is a bash command run from the repository root after `npm ci`, under `-e -o pipefail`. Every guard runs, even after a red.
- **Job and context:** both named `guards`. Behind this repo's caller job that is `baseline / guards`. The job is skipped when the list is empty.

**For the Engine half**, measured at `dev` `d7439e28bd`:

1. **The pin bump renames required contexts.** v0.1.84 reports ten `baseline / …` contexts. v1.1.0 reports three: `PR baseline`, `Skills materialized` and `guards` (#281/#283). The ruleset edit removes nine contexts: `PR base`, `PR body`, `Release ref`, `Skills version`, `Substrate size`, `Secrets`, `Commit authorship`, `Source comment archaeology` and `npm overrides`. It adds `baseline / PR baseline` and `baseline / guards`; `baseline / Skills materialized` keeps its name. The pin PR stays blocked until that edit, so the edit and the merge happen together. Three Engine PRs are open right now.
2. **`check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` has to learn the new mirror.** It credits only `jobs.*.steps[].run` in workflows whose `pull_request` trigger has no `types:` filter. `pr-baseline.yml` has a `types:` filter and a `uses:` job, so it never counts. Deleting `guard-ci-parity-lint.yml` in a scratch tree reds all **9** mirrored guards (`OK (14 lint-staged guards, 5 accepted client-only)` → `9 guard(s) invoked by lint-staged but by NO workflow`). The checker has to read the caller's `with.guards` entries as runs. It also has to accept a `types` list that contains `opened` and `synchronize`.
3. **`secrets-lint.yml` stays.** Its pull-request trigger only re-runs the workflow when the workflow itself is edited. Its real job is scanning `dev` pushes, which the data-sync pipeline needs, and the PR-only baseline cannot do that.
4. **`spec-retirement-lint` needs history.** The guard reads `origin/dev..HEAD`, but the `guards` job checks out at depth 1. Its entry has to fetch history before it runs.
5. **AC 4's reader lives in the Brain.** Engine CI can reach `PullRequestService` only by checking out the Brain, which #20328 retires. The same invariant holds statically if two things are true: the parity guard credits a `lint-staged` guard only when it runs inside the `guards` list, and it reds any other `dev`-PR workflow that runs one. That leaves one ruleset entry, read live and pasted into the PR (AC 2), and nothing else that can drift. This is a proposal: the ACs are Vega's.

## AC-3 receipt: a lint violation is merge-ineligible

The negative control was PR #20604 at `fcc5fc8d15`, read at 2026-11-08T19:50Z. It planted one lint violation: `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` grew past the size its front-door fingerprint declares. The pre-commit hook does not run that guard.

- **Merge state: `BLOCKED`.** `mergeable` reads `MERGEABLE`, so no conflict is involved; failing required checks block it.
- **`baseline / guards`, required since #20598, failed:** `front door fingerprint exited with 1` (declared 60831 bytes / 345 lines, actual 60932 / 347).
- **`unit`, already required, failed on the same drift:** `checkFrontDoorFingerprint.spec.mjs:118`, "the LIVE front door passes its own fingerprint check".
- **Everything else passed.** That includes `baseline / PR baseline`, once its first red, a missing `## Test Evidence` anchor in my own body, was fixed.

**Honest bound:** this lint was already mirrored by a live-tree unit spec, so the run shows the PR blocked but does not isolate `baseline / guards` as the only blocker. The ruleset closes that gap by construction. `baseline / guards` is a required context (live read, #20598 comment 6726039256), and any failing required context blocks a merge. A guard with no unit mirror, such as `check-theme-surfaces`, now has `baseline / guards` as its only carrier.

An isolating run would plant a `check-theme-surfaces` violation. That is an SCSS change, which starts a full e2e run (about 20 jobs) on the shared 20-slot pool, so I did not run it tonight. Say so if it's wanted.

#20604 is closed unmerged.
